references.text: Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket at the entrance to the tent of meeting. This shows that priests had the right to eat from the holy offerings.
Moses arranged the showbread on the table before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded. This is the first placement of the showbread that Aaron and his sons would later eat.
The remainder of the grain offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons, most holy among the Lord's fire offerings. The same principle applies: priests receive the holy portions.
What remains of the grain offering, Aaron and his sons shall eat. It must be eaten unleavened in a holy place. This confirms that priests are to eat the holy things in a holy place.
He may eat his God's food, both from the most holy and from the holy offerings. Even a priest with a physical defect could eat of the holy bread.

This shall belong to you from the most holy offerings that are not burned: all their grain offerings. You shall eat it in the most holy place. Confirms that the most holy things are to be eaten in a holy place.
David and his men ate the showbread when they were in need, even though it was meant only for priests. This shows how this law was applied in practice.
Jesus refers to David eating the showbread, which only priests were allowed to eat, to illustrate that mercy is more important than ceremonial laws.
Jesus refers to the incident with David and the showbread to defend his disciples' actions on the Sabbath.
Jesus uses the example of the showbread that David ate to teach about the Sabbath and God's mercy.
